high.title: Trump Declares US as 'Guardian of the Strait of Hormuz', Imposes 20% Tariff on All Cargo
high.summary: President Trump announced the US will act as 'Guardian of the Strait of Hormuz' and impose a 20% fee on all cargo passing through the strategic waterway, following the US-Israel conflict with Iran. This move has significant implications for global shipping costs and oil supply chains, which directly impact Indonesian energy prices and trade logistics. Legal and implementation questions remain unresolved, adding uncertainty to global commodity markets.

high.title: OJK Chief Reveals Why Online Gambling is Difficult to Eradicate in Indonesia
high.summary: OJK Chairwoman Friderica Widyasari Dewi identified six major challenges in combating online gambling in Indonesia, including rapid domain-switching by platform operators and the exploitation of digital technology within cross-border organized crime networks. The issue poses systemic risks to Indonesia's financial sector, as illegal funds flow through the banking system. This signals potential tightening of financial regulations and compliance requirements for Indonesian banks and fintech companies.

high.title: Capital Market Investors Now Surpass 30 Million
high.summary: OJK Chairwoman Friderica Widyasari Dewi announced that Indonesia's capital market investor base has surpassed 30 million people, up from 20 million in 2025 — a remarkable addition of 10 million investors in just half a year. This significant growth in retail participation is seen as a key buffer for domestic market stability. The milestone signals strong investor confidence and broadening financial inclusion in Indonesia.

high.title: OJK Regulation on IDX Demutualization to Be Released in September; BI and Danantara Set to Hold Exchange Shares
high.summary: OJK Chairwoman Friderica Widyasari Dewi confirmed that the regulatory framework (POJK) for the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) demutualization is targeted for completion in September 2026. Under the Financial Sector Development and Strengthening Law (P2SK), entities including the Ministry of Finance, Bank Indonesia, and BPI Danantara would be eligible to hold shares in the IDX. This is a landmark structural reform that could significantly reshape ownership and governance of Indonesia's capital markets.

high.title: Finance Minister Reveals Reason for Withdrawing Funds from State-Owned Banks; Bank Indonesia Signals 'Don't Interfere with Monetary Policy'
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa disclosed that he withdrew Budget Surplus Reserve (SAL) funds from state-owned banks (Himbara) after receiving signals from Bank Indonesia not to interfere with monetary policy. The withdrawal was intended to synchronize fiscal and monetary policy, with BI pledging to replace the liquidity. This raises important questions about banking sector liquidity conditions and coordination between fiscal and monetary authorities in Indonesia.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Has Plan to Repay High-Speed Rail Debt, Awaiting Asset Transfer to Ministry of Finance
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa revealed he already has a debt resolution scheme for the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Rail (Whoosh) project, but is waiting for PT KCIC assets to be formally transferred to the Ministry of Finance as ordered by President Prabowo. This is a significant fiscal matter as the high-speed rail project carries substantial state-related debt obligations. The resolution strategy could have material implications for state-owned enterprises and the government's balance sheet.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Reprimanded by Parliament Over Placement of Rp 400 Trillion Budget Surplus Funds in State Banks
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa faced criticism from the DPR Commission XI during a working session over his decision to place approximately Rp 400 trillion of the Budget Surplus Balance (SAL) into state-owned bank (Himbara) deposits. The funds are structured across different tenors: Rp 200 trillion until end-2026, Rp 100 trillion for three months, and Rp 100 trillion in flexible placements. This large-scale fund placement into state banks is highly significant for the banking sector liquidity and could influence interest rate dynamics.

high.title: Trump Blockades Iranian Ports, Threatens to Strike Power Plants and Bridges
high.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump has imposed a full blockade on all Iranian ports and threatened to attack power plants and bridges if Iran refuses to return to the negotiating table. Escalating U.S.-Iran tensions pose significant risks to global oil supply and energy prices, which directly impact Indonesia's trade balance, fuel subsidies, and inflation outlook. Indonesian investors should monitor potential commodity price spikes and their downstream effects on the Rupiah and the broader economy.

high.title: Finance Minister Purbaya Reveals Reason for Withdrawing Funds from State Banks; Bank Indonesia Signals 'Don't Interfere with Monetary Policy'
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa disclosed that the government's withdrawal of Excess Budget Balance (SAL) funds from state-owned banks (Himbara) was prompted by signals from Bank Indonesia asking the Treasury not to interfere with monetary policy. BI requested the government reduce its bank placements, promising to replace the liquidity through its own channels. This reveals a significant coordination dynamic between fiscal and monetary authorities that directly impacts banking sector liquidity and credit conditions.

high.title: US Dollar Still Holding at Rp 18,000 Level
high.summary: The US dollar slightly weakened against the Indonesian Rupiah, trading at Rp 18,065, down 26 points (0.14%) as of Wednesday morning. The dollar also weakened broadly against other major currencies including the Japanese Yen, Australian Dollar, British Pound, Euro, Singapore Dollar, and Chinese Yuan. The Rupiah's position at this level remains a key watch point for Indonesian investors and importers monitoring exchange rate risk.

high.title: Trump Blockades Iranian Ports, Threatens to Destroy Power Plants and Bridges
high.summary: US President Donald Trump has imposed a full blockade on all Iranian ports and threatened to strike Iran's power plants and bridges if Iran refuses to return to the negotiating table. The escalating US-Iran conflict raises significant concerns for global energy markets, as any disruption to Middle East oil supply chains could drive oil price volatility and impact Indonesia's energy import costs and trade balance. Indonesian investors should monitor potential commodity price spikes stemming from this geopolitical tension.

high.title: 9 Conglomerate Stocks Dominated by a Handful of Shareholders — Full List
high.summary: The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) has expanded its list of High Shareholding Concentration (HSC) stocks after incorporating a new 'price impact ratio' metric into its methodology, resulting in several major conglomerate-linked stocks being flagged. Notable inclusions are BREN (Prajogo Pangestu, 97.31% concentration), DSSA (Sinar Mas Group, 95.76%), and DCII (Otto Toto Sugiri, 99.96%). This development is critical as global index providers MSCI and FTSE Russell are set to remove HSC-categorized Indonesian stocks from their indices, which could trigger significant foreign capital outflows.

medium.title: Chicken and Egg Prices at Farm Level Begin to Recover — Here's the Reason
medium.summary: Indonesia's National Food Agency (Bapanas) reported that chicken and egg prices at the farm level are gradually recovering, driven by the resumption of the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program after the school holiday break and the end of the Javanese Suro month. The MBG program is proving to be a meaningful demand catalyst for poultry producers, stabilizing prices that had been under pressure. Investors in the poultry and food sector should note the program's measurable impact on commodity price recovery.

medium.title: Online Gambling Syndicate Modus Operandi: Paying Farmers and Housewives Rp 100,000–Rp 500,000 to Open Bank Accounts
medium.summary: The Indonesian government exposed a scheme where online gambling operators pay low-income individuals, including farmers and housewives, Rp 100,000–Rp 500,000 to open bank accounts used as illicit fund repositories. Minister of Digital Affairs Meutya Hafid called on banks to strengthen Know Your Customer (KYC) processes, especially in rural areas, to prevent account misuse. This development is likely to accelerate regulatory pressure on banks to enhance customer verification, increasing compliance costs across the sector.

medium.title: Budget Markup Found for Pickup Trucks in Village Cooperative Program — Finance Minister Responds
medium.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa responded to Indonesian Corruption Watch (ICW) findings alleging budget inflation in the procurement of pickup trucks for the Merah Putih Village Cooperative (Kopdes) program, stating that disbursements will only proceed after passing an audit. ICW has announced plans to report the alleged markup to the Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK), raising governance concerns over a major government rural economic program. This could affect investor confidence in government procurement processes and the broader village cooperative initiative.

medium.title: National Economic Council Meets President Prabowo at Hambalang, Discusses Economy and GovTech
medium.summary: The National Economic Council (DEN), led by Chairman Luhut Binsar Pandjaitan and members including Chatib Basri and Mari Elka Pangestu, met President Prabowo Subianto at his private residence in Hambalang, West Java. The council presented updates on national economic conditions, strategic recommendations for strengthening the economy amid global dynamics, and progress on GovTech digital transformation initiatives. The meeting underscores continued high-level attention to economic policy coordination and digital government reform.

medium.title: OJK Meets Airlangga, Requests Incentives for Gold ETF and New Financial Products
medium.summary: OJK Chairwoman Friderica Widyasari Dewi met with Coordinating Minister for the Economy Airlangga Hartarto to request tax or regulatory incentives for new financial sector products, including non-delivery gold ETFs. Gold ETFs are exchange-traded instruments that track gold prices without requiring physical ownership, offering a new accessible investment vehicle for retail investors. If approved, these incentives could boost product diversification in Indonesia's capital markets and attract a broader investor base.

medium.title: IDX Expands High Shareholding Concentration List; 51 Stocks Now Flagged
medium.summary: The Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) is adding 37 new stocks to its High Shareholding Concentration (HSC) list, bringing the total to 51 stocks, after introducing a new 'price-impact ratio' criterion for companies with market capitalization above IDR 10 trillion. HSC-listed stocks are subject to additional trading restrictions due to their ownership concentration risk. Investors in these stocks should be aware of potential liquidity and volatility implications under the revised regulatory framework.

medium.title: JCI Closes Marginally Higher at 6,039 Level
medium.summary: Indonesia's composite stock index (JCI/IHSG) closed slightly higher by 1.67 points (+0.03%) to 6,039.52, remaining in the 6,000 range. Trading volume reached 37.59 billion shares with a turnover of IDR 16.82 trillion across 2.81 million transactions. A total of 422 stocks advanced while 206 declined, reflecting a cautiously positive but largely flat market session.

medium.title: House Commission XI Chair Dismisses Claims That Danantara Bonds Are a Money Laundering Vehicle
medium.summary: House of Representatives Commission XI Chair Misbakhun pushed back against narratives labeling Danantara's Patriot Bond and Merah Putih Bond as money laundering instruments, arguing that bond purchases go through regulated intermediaries such as asset managers, securities firms, and bond brokers — all of which have their own KYC (Know Your Customer) processes. The controversy stems from the government's decision not to verify the source of funds for bond purchasers. This is relevant for investors considering these instruments, as the reputational and regulatory debate could affect demand and pricing.

medium.title: President Prabowo Sets IDR 500 Million Fee for Notaries Seeking to Transfer to Jakarta
medium.summary: President Prabowo Subianto has enacted Government Regulation No. 30/2026, setting a Non-Tax State Revenue (PNBP) fee of up to IDR 500 million for notaries wishing to transfer their jurisdiction to Jakarta, effective August 1, 2026. Lower fees apply for transfers to other city categories (IDR 50 million for Category B, IDR 25 million for Category C). This regulatory change affects the legal and property services sectors and may influence notarial service costs for businesses operating in Jakarta.

medium.title: State-Owned Shipyard PT Dok and Perkapalan Surabaya Declared Bankrupt; Danantara Plans Asset Takeover and Consolidation Under PT PAL
medium.summary: PT Dok dan Perkapalan Surabaya (DPS), a state-owned shipyard company, was declared bankrupt in early July 2026. Danantara's COO confirmed plans to take over DPS assets and consolidate them under PT PAL as part of a broader shipyard sector consolidation strategy. This marks a notable restructuring in Indonesia's state-owned maritime industry with potential implications for creditors and the broader BUMN ecosystem.

medium.title: 10 Village Associations Engaged to Socialize 'Merah Putih' Village Cooperative Program
medium.summary: Minister of Villages Yandri Susanto plans to partner with 10 village head associations to socialize the Merah Putih Village Cooperative (Kopdes) program, which is being rolled out across Indonesia using Village Funds. The program represents a significant rural economic development initiative backed by state resources. Businesses and investors in the rural economy, microfinance, and agricultural supply chain sectors should monitor the program's rollout as it could channel substantial village fund allocations.

medium.title: Danantara Bonds (Patriot Bond & Merah Putih Bond) Defended Against Money Laundering Allegations by House Commission XI Chair
medium.summary: House of Representatives Commission XI Chair Misbakhun pushed back against narratives branding Danantara's bond instruments — Patriot Bond and Merah Putih Bond — as vehicles for money laundering, arguing that standard bond market mechanisms (asset managers, securities firms, bond brokers with KYC procedures) inherently prevent such activity. The controversy stems from the government's decision not to verify the source of funds for bond purchases. Investor confidence in these instruments may be affected depending on how the public debate evolves.

medium.title: Prabowo Sets PNBP Fee of Up to IDR 500 Million for Notaries Relocating to Jakarta
medium.summary: President Prabowo has enacted Government Regulation No. 30/2026 setting non-tax state revenue (PNBP) fees of up to IDR 500 million for notaries seeking to transfer their jurisdiction to Jakarta, effective August 1, 2026. Lower fees apply for transfers to category B (IDR 50 million) and category C (IDR 25 million) regions. This regulatory change affects the legal and property services sector and may impact business costs for transactions requiring notarial services in Jakarta.

medium.title: Reports Emerge of Peruri Director Replacement by Retired Military Officer; Danantara COO Confirms Change Was Planned
medium.summary: Reports have surfaced that Dwina Septiani Wijaya, the current President Director of state-owned printing company Perum Peruri, is being replaced by a retired military (TNI) officer. Danantara COO Dony Oskaria confirmed that a leadership change at Peruri had been planned, though he had not yet seen the official announcement. As Peruri is a key state enterprise handling currency and document printing, leadership changes may signal shifts in strategic direction under Danantara's oversight.

medium.title: Danantara Interested in Taking Stake in Indonesia Stock Exchange — What Will Its Share Be?
medium.summary: Danantara CEO Rosan Roeslani confirmed the sovereign wealth fund's interest in becoming a shareholder of the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) as part of the government's stock exchange demutualization initiative. OJK (Financial Services Authority) is targeting completion of the demutualization regulations by September, aiming to open IDX ownership to the public and improve governance, transparency, and accountability. Rosan noted that SWF participation in stock exchanges is common globally and could boost market confidence among capital market participants.

medium.title: Indonesian Stocks Delisted from MSCI and FTSE — IDX Chief: We Prefer Stocks Enter the Right Way
medium.summary: IDX President Director Jeffrey Hendrik stated that the exchange prefers Indonesian stocks to be included in global indices through proper and legitimate means, following the disclosure of High Shareholding Concentration (HSC) stocks. Both MSCI and FTSE Russell have indicated they will remove HSC-categorized Indonesian stocks from their constituent lists, a move that reflects long-standing criticism from global index providers and institutional investors about concentrated ownership practices. The IDX's stance signals a commitment to improving market structure quality over short-term index inclusion benefits.
